'According to the Puranas, their dynasty was brought to an end by the Satavahanas in 28 BCE'; 'The Puranas suggest that the last king of the Kanva dynasty was killed by Balipuccha, who founded the Andhra dynasty,' though the page notes a lack of numismatic and archaeological evidence. 'After the defeat ... the Magadha empire came to an end.' notes:
Cliopatria row Kanva Dynasty -66..-28, 3 shapes. Two pages opened (budget 1-2). The page gives no area, so no ratio.

Departures from Cliopatria: start -73 (page) instead of -66, with a new keyframe on the Shunga outline for -73..-67.

Not settled: (a) Kanva as a rename of the Shunga state (usurpation by a minister, same capitals, identical Cliopatria cells): see the note in shunga-empire. (b) The Kanva extent: no page gives one; the Cliopatria shape is the Shunga outline. (c) The Mitra dynasty of Kaushambi ('Magadha later came under the hegemony of the Mitra dynasty', 1st century BCE to 2nd century CE) and the Panchala Mitras (see panchala-kingdom) are not in Cliopatria; a dossier would need a page on them. (d) The end: the Puranas' 28 BCE is the only date, and the page doubts the Balipuccha story; Cliopatria agrees on -28.
Rulers are the page's regnal list (Puranic years); the reigns above (9+14+12+10) sum to the 45 years from 73 to 28 BCE (the Satavahana page quotes the Brahmanda Purana: 'the four Kanvas will rule the earth for 45 years').
